clue.text: Not yet decided on flying?

definitions.meaning: a plan still pending or unsettled is said to be up ...
something airborne, aloft above the ground, is literally up in the sky

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for an unresolved matter, and also the literal phrase for being airborne, aloft above the ground.

clue.text: Small number attempt to entertain a public official

parts.note: NO is the short form of number

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them inside, so the attempt word contains the letter

parts.note: a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A minor group of people make an effort to host a government officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal official authorised to witness and certify documents and oaths.

clue.text: He'd put in little work, yet had expectations

indicators.note: the short work is put in the middle of the contraction

parts.note: the contraction taken as its letters without the apostrophe
OP, short for opus, is a work of music

explanation.surface: A man who did little but expected a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: To have hoped means to have expected or wished for something to come.

clue.text: Enter game play, making contract

indicators.note: to play with letters is to rearrange them

explanation.surface: Joining a sports match by signing a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract is a legally binding deal or accord between parties.

clue.text: Dish one has possibly to stir round

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be ordered another way

parts.note: a round shape resembles the letter O

explanation.surface: A rice dish one may have to keep stirring as it cooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one has' is just padding for the surface. The anagram of TO STIR plus O gives the dish, which famously needs constant stirring.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian rice dish cooked slowly with stock, a classic example of a dish.

clue.text: Man on watch around Beachy Head

indicators.note: the word for being on watch goes around the next piece

parts.note: someone on watch is alert, keeping a lookout

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of the clue word Beachy

explanation.surface: A coastguard keeps lookout near the famous chalk cliff on the Sussex coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Beachy Head is a chalk headland in Sussex, England; here 'Head' just takes its first letter. 'Watch' also hints at the albert, a Victorian watch chain, a nice distraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert is a common male first name, so a man may be called that.

clue.text: A look of being indifferent

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: Someone gives a look that shows they couldn't care less.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one unbroken phrase, 'a look of', but it splits into three short words; LO is an archaic interjection meaning 'look'.
explanation.definitionFit: Distant and uninvolved, showing no interest or warmth toward others.

clue.text: Bit of money firm's directors may be hoarding

parts.note: a bill is a banknote in American usage
a company's directors make up its board

explanation.surface: A company's executives are stashing away cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hoarding' is not stockpiling but a noun: the British word for a large outdoor advertising board.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoarding in British English is a large board for posters and advertisements beside roads.

clue.text: Erred badly when about to finish, so gave up

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, i.e. around, the finish word
something done badly is bungled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an end is a finish

explanation.surface: Someone who went wrong near the end surrendered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' turns ERRED into RERED, which goes 'about' END as R...ERED.
explanation.definitionFit: To render can mean to hand over or surrender, as in rendering unto Caesar.

clue.text: Translating Proust may produce it!

indicators.note: translating turns the author's name into something else, so his letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Reading a French novelist in translation will send you into a daze.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a joke that the long-winded novels of Marcel Proust leave a reader dazed.
explanation.definitionFit: A dazed, near-unconscious state is what the clue jokingly says the novelist's long books produce in a reader.

clue.text: Glowering milk producer's cast out

indicators.note: the word for cast sits on the outside of the milk producer

parts.note: to cast something is to throw or sling it
a cow is the farm animal producing milk

explanation.surface: A dairy cow that is sulking gets thrown out of the herd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' says the throw word goes on the outside, wrapping the farm animal, rather than meaning something is ejected.
explanation.definitionFit: Glowering and frowning angrily are near synonyms, both describing a dark, sullen look.

clue.text: Inclination to fade away, in general

indicators.note: the fading word is placed inside the general's name

parts.note: Ulysses S. Grant was a US Civil War general
to die away is to fade gradually

explanation.surface: A general tends to let things quietly fade away.
explanation.definitionFit: A slope or incline; inclination and gradient both mean the steepness of a rise.

clue.text: They may be spun — to make briefs?

indicators.note: the answer, once spun, is rearranged to make the clue word briefs, so that word's letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: Threads are spun on a loom to weave underpants.
explanation.walkthrough: This is really a reverse anagram: spinning (rearranging) the answer would make BRIEFS. Working backwards, rearrange BRIEFS to find it.
explanation.definitionFit: Threads of wool or cotton are spun into yarn, so strands of that kind may be spun.

clue.text: Is most prominent, but badly impersonated

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mimic who does a poor job still steals the show.
explanation.definitionFit: To predominate is to dominate or be the most noticeable among others.

clue.text: 19th-century war zone writer almost isolated

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: insular means cut off, isolated like an island

explanation.surface: A war correspondent was cut off in a battle area long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The Peninsular War (1807-14) was fought by Britain against Napoleon on the Iberian Peninsula.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iberian land mass was the theatre of the Peninsular War against Napoleon.

clue.text: One close to home no longer joking

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
near means close to
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: Someone living nearby has stopped kidding around.
explanation.definitionFit: Being serious and sincere, the opposite of jesting or kidding.

clue.text: They travel with others to work

definitions.text: They travel with others to work

parts.words: They travel with others to work
parts.note: seems to describe commuters, but means guides who travel with tour groups as their job

explanation.definitionFit: Tour guides who accompany holiday groups abroad are employed to travel with them.

clue.text: Out of sight; out of mind?

definitions.meaning: beyond a corner in the road, hidden from view
slang for mad, having lost one's mind

explanation.definitionFit: Literal sense: past a curve and hidden; British slang sense: crazy, out of one's mind.

clue.text: Former spouse called, in high spirits

parts.note: an ex is a former husband or wife
cited means called, as to appear in court

explanation.surface: An ex-partner phoned and sounded thrilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrilled and eager, full of energy and enthusiasm.

clue.text: In time, beat up relative

indicators.note: the reversed word is placed inside the time word

parts.note: an age is a period of time

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them

explanation.surface: Over time a family member got beaten up.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnate means related through the male line, a kinsman on the father's side.

clue.text: It's quickly torn asunder in Post Office

indicators.note: the scrambled word goes inside the post office letters
torn asunder means ripped apart, so the letters of torn are scattered

explanation.surface: A parcel gets ripped apart quickly at the sorting office.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal adverb borrowed from Spanish and Italian meaning promptly, right away.

clue.text: Something in the air makes one put on weight? On the contrary

indicators.note: in a down clue, put on means placed above
the opposite holds: the weight goes on top of one

parts.note: oz is the abbreviation for ounce, a unit of weight
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something makes a person gain weight, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'one put on weight' sets one above the weight; 'On the contrary' flips that, so the weight goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A form of oxygen found in the atmosphere, notably the upper layer shielding Earth.

clue.text: Deportment of unusual air and grace

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Someone carries themselves with a rare elegance and poise.
explanation.definitionFit: Deportment is how one carries oneself, posture and bearing, the same sense as the way one holds oneself.

clue.text: I dine out in self-reliant company

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A self-sufficient person eats at a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: An independent firm, especially a record label or film studio, not owned by a major.

clue.text: Scale of air force taking fine French stronghold

parts.note: beau is French for fine or handsome
a fort is a fortified stronghold

explanation.surface: An RAF base takes over a handsome old French castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air force' is not the RAF: it means the force of moving air, wind. 'taking' just links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beaufort scale is the standard measure of wind strength, from calm to hurricane.

clue.text: Attach and aim a listening device

parts.note: an end is a goal or aim
the ear is the body's organ for hearing

explanation.surface: Someone fixes a bug and points it to eavesdrop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attach' here means to make fond, as in attaching someone's affection to you.
explanation.definitionFit: To win someone's affection, to make them attached or fond of you.

clue.text: Executor's first to divulge what's left in the will

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, here of Executor's

parts.note: to state something is to declare or reveal it

explanation.surface: An executor reveals at the start what a dead person bequeathed.
explanation.definitionFit: The property and assets a dead person leaves, which the will disposes of.

clue.text: Couldn't choose, and did without there

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside, so did goes around there

explanation.surface: An indecisive person managed without going to some place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense 'outside': DID surrounds THERE as DI...D.
explanation.definitionFit: To dither is to hesitate, wavering between options and failing to decide.
